stories.title: Fed hikes 25 bp to 3.75–4% — first increase since July 2023

facts.text: FOMC (Wed 14:00 EDT / 20:00 Berlin): benchmark rate +25 bp to a 3.75–4.00% range — first hike in more than three years; vote unanimous including Chair Kevin Warsh (CNN; Fed release).
Statement: action aims at a “timelier return” to the 2% inflation goal; officials’ projections pencil in another hike by year-end (CNN).
Context: inflation rebound tied to the Iran war/energy shock plus AI-buildout concerns; August CPI firmed; labor market (unemployment ~4.1%) seen able to take tighter policy (CNN).
10-year Treasury already >5% Tue (highest close since 2007) — markets had priced some of the tightening ahead of the decision (CNN).

stories.whyItMatters: Warsh’s first big rate move restarts a hiking cycle after three years — and Superstonk flagged the Fed release the same evening.

stories.title: Ukraine: drone strike on civilian minibus near Nikopol kills ≥5

facts.text: Dnipropetrovsk governor Oleksandr Hansha: Russian drone hit a civilian Linienbus near Nikopol — ≥5 dead, ≥7 injured; photo of bloodied bus posted (tagesschau ~18:40).
Regional council chair Mykola Lukaschuk: strike deliberately targeted a Kleinbus with civilians on everyday routes; no Russian comment yet (tagesschau).
Same day: drone hit passenger train Kyiv–Mykolaiv (all 170 passengers evacuated, train burned); locomotive hit in Kovel (Volyn) (tagesschau).
Zelenskyy (Telegram): “Akt der Barbarei”; calls for harder US/EU sanctions — “kein Zeitpunkt, den Druck zu verringern” (tagesschau).

stories.whyItMatters: Fresh civilian-transport targeting on the southern front — same evening as Zelenskyy’s push against any sanctions easing.

stories.title: Aramco: half East-West capacity via bypass within days; full ~6 weeks

facts.text: Bloomberg (person familiar): Saudi Aramco bypassing a damaged East-West Pipeline section — ~half capacity targeted within days; full capability ~six weeks (TT/Bloomberg).
Outage after Sept 10 drone attacks had threatened exports on the ~7 mb/d nameplate Red Sea lifeline while Hormuz stays disrupted; London crude cited above $107 (TT/Bloomberg).

Aramco/ministry did not comment; Aramco also ramped sales outside Hormuz (~20 mb to Asian refiners for Sep/Oct liftings, per traders) while Europe faces delays (Orlen buying replacements) (TT/Bloomberg).
Material upgrade vs afternoon’s BBC Verify 4–6 week pumping-station repair framing — partial Red Sea path may reopen sooner if the bypass works.

stories.whyItMatters: First concrete partial-restart path after Yanbu loadings paused — could ease the acute European cargo squeeze if the bypass works.

stories.title: Pistorius–Hegseth MoU: deeper US–German defense-industry tie-up

facts.text: In Washington, BMVg Boris Pistorius and US SecDef Pete Hegseth signed an Absichtserklärung to deepen defense-industry cooperation (ZDF/dpa).
BMVg: challenges need a “robust … eng verzahnte Verteidigungsindustriebasis” on both sides of the Atlantic — frame for development, production, licensed manufacturing, maintenance (ZDF).
Also: strengthen supply chains, review tech-transfer rules, expand R&D; Hegseth praised Germany’s NATO spending trajectory toward the 5% pledge (ZDF).
Context: US already agreed Tomahawk sales; Pistorius also flagged F-35 and Patriot missile production in Germany (ZDF).

stories.whyItMatters: Political framework for industrial catch-up — not a procurement contract, but the densest US–DE armaments MoU of this reset.

stories.title: BGH: consumers can use BGB to stop illegal data handoffs

facts.text: BGH VI ZR 144/23: GDPR does not block German BGB Unterlassungsansprüche against unauthorized personal-data transfers to third parties (heise).
Case: online shop cloud setup forwarded the shopper’s browser (IP + usage data) straight to third-party servers without consent; plaintiff sought a future stop order (heise).

OLG Frankfurt had said GDPR is exhaustive and offers no standalone Unterlassung without simultaneous Löschung; BGH overturned, citing CJEU that national preventive remedies strengthen GDPR effectiveness (heise).
Routes left open: general personality right / informational self-determination and §§ 823, 1004 BGB; remitted to OLG for a new merits hearing (heise).

stories.whyItMatters: Gives German consumers a clearer civil stop-button against shop/third-party data pipelines — beyond GDPR erasure fights.

stories.title: Mistral × Mozilla: Firefox Smart Window beta runs on Mistral

facts.text: Joint announcement: Firefox Smart Window (beta) AI browsing assistant now powered by Mistral models — FR + North America first; UK and Germany expected later this year (Mistral).
Privacy pitch: conversations not saved on Mozilla servers by default; Mistral agrees to zero data retention (Mistral).
Framing: open-weight models + open distribution; regional-language fine-tunes so answers feel local (Mistral; quotes from Mensch + Mozilla CEO Enzor-DeMeo).

stories.whyItMatters: Puts a European open-weight lab inside Firefox’s AI surface — a rare browser-side alternative to US closed stacks.
